newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ENGLAND INTERNATIONAL ANDERTON FACES ANOTHER OPERATION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ENGLAND INTERNATIONAL ANDERTON FACES ANOTHER OPERATION.

text.p: England international forward Darren Anderton will have surgery next week in a bid to cure the latest in a series of injury problems which have disrupted his career for both Tottenham and his country.
Anderton plans to enter hospital on Tuesday for a hernia operation which will rule him out of England's World Cup qualifier against Poland at Wembley on October 9.
He said: "It is similar to a hernia problem I had when I first joined Spurs. I had an operation then and that sorted it out for good but it did mean six weeks out."
Anderton made only six premier league starts for Tottenham last season because of a persistent groin injury.

He regained fitness in time to play in all five of England's matches in the European Championship finals, but then had to miss the opening World Cup qualifier in Moldova with a recurrence of the hernia problem.
"It usually starts to ache in the second half of games after a lot of twisting and turning, and has been restricting my running to some extent," he said.
"You are obviously aware of the injury the whole time and end up losing maybe a yard of pace."

The unlucky 24-year-old picked up another injury in Wednesday night's 3-0 league cup victory over Preston. After scoring Spurs' opening goal, he limped off in the 41st minute with a dead leg above the right knee.
Spurs assistant manager Roger Cross said: "Providing he recovers from the dead leg he will play against Manchester United on Sunday, and then go into hospital next week."
